correctness.rationale: For p>2, 2-cycle gap d∈(0,p) satisfies q=Qp(d)=p+d coth(d/2−artanh(d/p)), increasing from p²/(p−2) to ∞ on 0<d<d∞. Thus exactly one prime two-cycle in the asserted regime, not merely computational detection. Let d∞=2θ, p=2θ coth θ=P(θ). Derivatives P′>0,P″>0 give limiting M∞=(1−p)²−d∞²=1−2θP′(θ), crossing −1 once where θP′=1; implicit expansion in t=1/q gives d=d∞−K/q+O(q⁻²), M=M∞+C/q+O(q⁻²). At crossing C=4(p³−3p²+4p−1)>0, M∞′=−2(1+θP″/P′)<0, so S=−C/M∞′≈6.745591544665048>0. Sign of multiplier locally yields attracting/repelling sides. No claim of nondegenerate flip bifurcation at equality. Scripts inspect actual equations; numerical roots only corroborate analytic IFT.

Their inspected full main parameter discussions and numerical continuation do not state or imply first asymptotic coefficient S. Mathematically distinct stronger coverage was searched, not found.
